## Body

Security verdict, #306 (F249), ROUND 2 (final, C34) at 89a82bf8ec10ca7ba8902f2070df7efb8560542f: PASS WITH NOTES. Static review of the change alone (git diff 8af888e2^ 8af888e2). CI at this head: check(22), check(24), rust-lint and rust-test succeeded; delivers succeeded on its latest run (an earlier delivers run was cancelled and superseded); CLEAN. I ran no live canary and no build.

My round-1 notes:
- S306-N1 CLOSED. unisphere seat_status now sets model_switch_pending when the status lists "model.pending_switch" as unknown, and SeatStatus::unknown() sets it to true. The test an_undecided_switch_reads_as_pending covers both the undecided and the decided case. I checked the SDK side: derive() drops the name from `unknown` only when pending_known is true, so a decided no-switch still reads false. A same-millisecond tie is still invisible on the pij side. That's acceptable: the footer agreement check catches it whenever the footer already shows the new model.
- S306-N2 CLOSED as asked. runtime_model refuses with Disagree (details.native_model and details.footer_model) when an OMP footer names a model that the native selector's own catalog row does not show. omp_model_shows matches only inside that one row (selector, id, name, or the name with "Claude " removed), so names shared across providers can't make the check pass or fail falsely.

Crafted footer. The footer parse (unchanged from round 1) answers None for no model segment, two segments, a glued glyph or no-model, and None skips the agreement check. So the check is only as good as the footer, which is the harness's own render and fails closed. A footer that a seat itself steers into naming the native model only removes a cross-check. It can't create a pass the native record didn't already give. Under C33 (the trust boundary is the user account) that is the accepted residual. The canary stays a misattribution check, not proof against a lying seat.

Freshness. Round 2 drops the comparison of observation.facts.native_session_id with current.harness_session, so observe_bind now gets no session id. I checked adapter.rs observe_bind_with_model_lookup: native_session_id is copied straight from the argument into the facts, so the old comparison could never fail. Removing it loses nothing. The incarnation is still bound by the pane-process subtree check and the non-empty bound session, and native is read only for seat.harness_session. The doc now says this correctly ("process, bound session and pane").

Catalog-outage question:
- S306-003 (LOW, new, non-blocking): the agreement check fails open on a catalog error. `if let Ok(false) = catalog.shows(..)` treats any Err as agreement, and the test native_evidence_needs_no_footer_resolution pins that. An Err covers: omp models failing, its 5 s OMP_TIMEOUT expiring under fleet load, unparseable output, or the native selector missing from the inventory.
- So a stale native record after a role switch the record doesn't see (R306-001: smol, slow, temporary, fallback or prewalk), combined with a catalog Err, passes on the stale model. The seat's next call would run the footer's model. That is a real gap in the misattribution property, but it needs both conditions at once.
- It is also looser than main. There, a footer naming a model was always resolved through the catalog and an Err refused, though main refused every OMP canary anyway.
- A missing selector rarely matters. Native is provider/model from the response, which normally equals a catalog selector. If it doesn't, native usually fails the expect/bound comparison and the canary refuses anyway.
- Fix: when the footer names a model and shows() errs, refuse with the catalog error in the details (fail closed). This costs nothing extra: the canary still makes one omp.models launch, and only when the footer names a model. A canary refused during an outage is a safe failure and can be retried.
- Acceptable to merge as is, given the low likelihood and C33, if the PM records it. Otherwise fix it before merge.

Launch and cost (security view): unchanged from round 1. The site is omp.models, launched through program::launch by absolute path with fixed argv (models --json --no-extensions), no footer text in argv or env, a 5 s timeout, and it runs on spawn_blocking off the reactor. It runs at most once per OMP canary, and only when the footer names a model: resolve and shows never both run, because they are exclusive branches of runtime_model. Nothing runs per tick or per seat.
